comparison: Both strongly support findings about repeat number variability (C131-C134). OpenEval notes the limited sample size (5 of 7 birds) while peer reviewers describe the analysis as thorough and well-supported without raising sample size concerns.

Both address species differences speculation (C91, C138). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental support, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the extrapolation without challenge, accepting the logic despite its speculative nature.

Both support preservation of syllable acoustic structure (C140-C143). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative similarity analyses and statistical tests, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm that lesions 'do not affect syllable acoustic structure' with compelling evidence.

Both address mMAN-lMAN contrast (C107-C109). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental support for distributed control claims, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the comparison, calling the opposite effects 'striking and important.'

Both support mMAN's role in sequencing (C14, C90, C104). OpenEval finds conclusions reasonable and appropriately framed, while peer reviewers describe this as 'a very important and surprising result' with compelling evidence.

Both support motor exploration interpretation (C105-C106). OpenEval notes this is appropriately framed as speculative, while peer reviewers support the parallel to lMAN's role in generating vocal variability.

Both support increased sequential variability findings (C10, C79-C80, C84-C85). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple analyses with statistical support, while peer reviewers call this 'exactly the opposite result from what would be predicted' and 'very important.'

Both support effects on multiple organizational levels (C116, C129). OpenEval notes appropriate statistical support and valid inference contradicting simple functional division, while peer reviewers affirm increased variability within chunks as part of thorough analysis.

Both address zebra finch comparison (C136). OpenEval rates explanation as UNCERTAIN lacking direct experimental support, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the contextualization, noting particular interest given previous zebra finch studies.

Both address rejection of simple functional division (C117). OpenEval supports this as valid inference from data showing mMAN affects multiple levels, while peer reviewers implicitly support by accepting mMAN's contribution to multiple aspects of syntax.

Both support preservation of syllable types and structure (C9, C83, C89). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence with adequate sample size and controls, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm lesions did not grossly disrupt acoustic structure.

Both support increased transition entropy (C12, C85). OpenEval includes this in converging evidence with statistical support, while peer reviewers specifically mention increased transition entropy as evidence of syntactic variability effects.

Both address temporal aspects (C81-C82). OpenEval provides detailed support with statistical tests, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of well-designed experiments without detailed discussion.

Both support broader implications about frontal systems (C15). OpenEval finds conclusions reasonable from experimental data, while peer reviewers support interpretation showing distinct frontal systems have distinct functions.

Both support chunk-level variability (C11, C86). OpenEval includes this in converging evidence from multiple analyses, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm variability within stereotyped chunks as part of excellent analysis.

Both address song production continuation (C88). OpenEval documents preservation in supplementary figures, while peer reviewers implicitly support by noting lesions affected sequencing but not whether song was produced.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims about lesion procedures and verification (C55-C64) as SUPPORTED with detailed documentation, though notes wide age range as potential unaddressed limitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates song analysis methodology (C65-C78) as SUPPORTED, noting use of current best practices (UMAP, TweetyNet) and appropriate methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates nonsignificant trend claim (C146) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of statistical support by definition. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Peer reviewers support utility of Bengalese finch model system (C16, C26), highlighting complex transition structures enabled the discovery. No corresponding OpenEval evaluation found.
